children: AutoZone recorded higher fiscal fourth-quarter sales, boosted by new store openings as well as growth at its existing locations.
The auto-parts retailer said it expects its growth to continue in the year ahead, forecasting an acceleration across each of its regions.
Shares were up 3.1% to $2,890 in premarket trading.

AutoZone posted a fiscal fourth-quarter profit of $931.6 million, compared with $837 million a year earlier. Earnings per share were $56.05, compared with the $54.08 expected by analysts polled by FactSet. The company said its margins improved in part due to tariff refunds.
Revenue rose 5.6% to $6.59 billion, compared with analyst estimates of $6.7 billion.

The top-line increase was helped by AutoZone's expanded footprint of 8,031 locations as of the end of the quarter, up from 7,657 a year earlier. The company opened new stores in each of its geographies, including the U.S., Mexico and Brazil.

Same-store sales, or those from stores open at least a year, rose 2.7%, compared with analyst estimates for a 3.8% increase. On a constant-currency basis, the figure was up 1.5%, with an uptick at both domestic and international locations.
Chief Executive Phil Daniele said the company contended with a difficult selling environment in the first half of the quarter, but that sales results strengthened in the back half.
The company is well positioned for sales growth in the year ahead, Daniele said.
"Based on the data we have, we continued to gain share and we expect sales in each of the three countries in which we operate to accelerate in the new fiscal year," Daniele said.
